candidates.label: Galatia (region and Roman province, label point)
candidates.support: Galatia was, per Wikidata, the highland area of central Asia Minor; Celtic (Gaulish) migrants had migrated to Asia Minor by 278 BC, and the region was organized as a Roman province in 25 BC (per bib:zondervan-who-were-galatians). The label point is Wikidata's coordinate for the region; Pleiades' 'Galatia' province/region label (a separate entity from the late Roman 'Galatia I' record) is about 90 km away, a reasonable margin for a region label.

summary.text: Galatia was both an ethnic region of Celtic settlers in the highlands of central Asia Minor and, from 25 BC, a much larger Roman province of the same name that also reached south to cities such as Antioch in Pisidia, Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe. Scholars are divided, without a clear consensus, on which of these Paul meant by 'the assemblies of Galatia' in his letter: the 'North Galatian' view holds he wrote to ethnic-Galatian congregations in the province's northern, Celtic-settled area, while the 'South Galatian' view holds he wrote to the congregations he founded on his first journey in the province's southern cities; this project takes neither side.

history.text: The Roman province of Galatia was formed in 25 BC and administered from the provincial capital Ancyra (modern Ankara); in its larger first-century extent it also included southern regions such as Pisidia and Lycaonia, before Vespasian detached most of Pisidia in AD 74.
